Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Sequester is ready to move forward with a small pilot that will process PHI-bound clinical notes and generate anonymized summaries. Legal has flagged two key constraints: (1) data must remain in a customer-dedicated environment (no multi-tenant sharing), and (2) audit logs must be retained for 7 years.

We need a short write-up comparing: (A) Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) and (B) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for the pilot, with estimated sizing and cost delta for an initial 3-month pilot.

Traffic profile (expected): 50 concurrent users at peak, 10 requests/sec steady-state, average input length 1.2k tokens, expected 300 tokens generated per request. Model target: a robust 70B family model (we're open to quantized variants).

Can you include the operational tradeoffs (SLA, backups, support path), security controls we will need to enable, and a recommended fallback if we hit burst >2x projections?

Ava

Sequester Therapeutics

Ava — thanks, we've kicked off an internal sizing pass. High level notes attached and a rough capacity modeling sheet. Key assumptions listed below.

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Peak concurrency: 50 users -> we model 50 concurrent active sessions, 10 req/s steady state.
- Model: 70B quantized to 4-bit (~35GB effective model memory) with KV cache for efficient calls.
- Latency SLO target: 400–700 ms p50 for streaming token start, p95 under 1.8s.

Private (VPC / on-prem) path — summary:
- Minimum starting footprint: 4 x A100-equivalent GPU instances (or 6 x 80GB Ampere for redundancy)
- Rationale: active shard + 1 replica for high availability + 1 warm spare for maintenance/bursting.
- Ops: Customer-managed network, we provide platform package + installation guide. Redwood provides remote support VPN for ESCALATION and KMS integration.

Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) path — summary:
- Minimum starting footprint: 3 x 80GB GPUs in a reserved pool (shared by only this tenant logically), autoscale to 6 during business hours via burst credits.
- Rationale: lower up-front onboarding, Redwood manages patching and backups; isolated tenancy but still under Redwood control plane.

I've attached the capacity_modeling_sheet.xlsx with cost delta and a first-pass MPA (sequester_mpa_draft.pdf).

Next steps: Evelyn to add network & audit log specifics; Priyom to outline canary + rollback plan.

—Karthik

Ava / team — technical clarification and recommended configuration attached. Summary below.

Workload characteristics that matter: average generation length, session stickiness (reuse of KV cache), and encryption-at-rest throughput for audit logs. From your inputs: KV cache reuse expected ~65% across conversational sessions.

Sizing detail (recommendation):
- Private on-prem option:
  - 4 x 80GB GPUs (NVIDIA H100 or equivalent) across 2 racks.
  - Node sizing: 512 GB RAM, 48 vCPU, 2 x 10Gbps uplink per node.
  - Expected throughput: ~20 req/s per GPU with the quantized 70B; with 4 GPUs ~80 req/s sustained, p95 latency ~1.2s.
  - Audit & retention: Shipable audit agent writes to local object store replicated to customer-managed long-term archive (S3 Glacier or equivalent).

- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pool):
  - 3 x 80GB GPUs reserved; autoscale policy to +3 GPUs for business hours bursts (via burst credits).
  - Node sizing: we manage OS + drivers; network egress controlled via VPC peering and private endpoints.
  - Throughput: ~60–70 req/s sustained with autoscale active; p95 latency slightly better due to optimized kernel stack.

Operational tradeoffs:
- Private: strongest control for compliance (data never leaves customer-controlled networking), higher procurement lead time and higher initial CAPEX/OPEX for hardware ops, predictable network latency inside customer DC.
- Dedicated: faster time-to-live, Redwood handles patching and SLAs; slightly reduced control over physical topology but still supports customer KMS and audit streams exported to the customer's S3.

Fallback strategy for >2x burst: enable cross-region fallback to a warmed dedicated pool (Redwood-managed) with encrypted transit and short-lived KV cache warming. This adds cost but preserves availability.

Request: procurement constraints (DocuSign, SOC2 evidence windows), and an expected pilot start date so we can lock the provisioning runway.

Evelyn Hart
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachment: private_vs_dedicated_technote.pdf
